problem: Personalized object-goal navigation agents lack long-term memory, so they cannot reuse locations found in earlier successful episodes. This causes redundant exploration in repetitive tasks and lowers path efficiency.
motivation: In household settings, different users repeatedly ask for their own object instances, so past successes are valuable priors. Without memory, each episode starts from scratch and wastes steps.
key_idea: Store user-conditioned object instances and their historically successful locations in a User-Goal-Location Graph, and retrieve them via Memory-augmented Chain-of-Thought during planning to cut redundant exploration.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims memory reuse raises SPL while SR stays stable, which suggests the gain comes from shorter paths rather than from finding more goals.
method: User-Goal-Location Graph (UGG): a long-term memory module that structurally stores user-conditioned object instances and their historically successful locations, and is dynamically updated.
Memory-CoT: during planning, the reasoning mechanism actively retrieves relevant historical experiences and injects them as explicit variables into the chain-of-thought.
MA-USON: builds on a personalized object navigation (USON-style) pipeline, with memory-guided planning driving the subsequent navigation policy.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (likely an LLM/VLM planner)

results: The abstract reports that MA-USON improves SPL while keeping SR stable on multi-user personalized object navigation tasks. No numbers or baselines are given in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the details of the setup, benchmark and baselines are unknown.
Memory relies on earlier successful episodes, so it likely helps only in repetitive tasks and may not help on first-time goals.
